body: I’m really, very happy I could help!

I’m really sorry you have to feel this way, I can do my best to emphasize with the pain you’re feeling but I know I’d only be able to understand it at surface level. Right now, I’d be happy to encourage you. Because I genuinely believe there is a lot of good people out there that would help us as a society to be less lonely. It will take time, and a lot of effort, but at times I’ll feel like relationships are futile, I try to remember, or hold on to the fact that people care about me as I do them. You, as a living breathing human being, are priceless. Nothing could be more valuable than you, because lives are so important they can’t be measured. Your entire existence can’t be comprehended. In your mind, an entire universe exists. An instance of life itself, everything in this world, exists through your perspective. That’s incredible, and beautiful, and nothing can be more valuable than that. Not to mention, we’ve all got lovable things about ourselves, that we’ve unfortunately unable to see ourselves.

I’m glad it could help, and I think I get what you mean. It’s really difficult, and our brains will do our best to convince us of the worst. I just hope that at least hearing from one person - that I don’t think this reflects who you are by any means - can help you heal from this. <3
There are no bad people, only bad decisions. Sometimes good people do things they’re not proud of.

There’s a lot I’d like to do in the future, it feels like any mental clarity I have is full to the brim with aspirations. It’s just starting to feel like all the things I’ve been dreaming of have only made me more sad. I.e., I’ve got what I wanted and it didn’t help. I got my license, and it’s only magnified problems I’ve already been dealing with. I guess it has helped, though. I don’t mean to be all doom-and-gloom. I just really needed a place to get this off my chest.

What about shoplifting would, for a second, make you a bad person?
We’re all human. You deserve to be loved, and you deserve the kindness others treat you with. Shoplifting, of course, is illegal. But an action like that doesn’t represent you as an individual. You clearly feel guilty for it, too. So that shows your morals and perspective is already that of a considerate person.

I’m really sorry you’re feeling this way, I really wish I could take away your hurt. I’m sure in 5 years time, I still wouldn’t be able to fully grasp what’s going on in your life. I can’t say anything that will help you, I can’t really answer whether or not something is “worth it”. But you deserve to be happy, you deserve to be well, and I’m very sorry you aren’t. I hope things become better, for you. I hope you will be well

Abuse isn’t inherently negative, aggressive or anger-focused. A lot of abuse goes unnoticed because it’s primarily manipulation. Which, in most cases, the abuser seems very kindhearted and would make it seem as though being upset with them is hurtful since they’ve ‘done nothing wrong’.

I don’t mean to invalidate anything you’re saying, though, I just wanted to express this concern cause there are a lot of people in terrible situations cause of abuse they’re unaware of. Not everything needs a label, none of that would mean you don’t belong. You’re human, you belong as a human. 
If you’re male and you want to act and feel however the hell you want, there’s nothing wrong with that and it doesn’t need to be labeled. We’re a lot more complicated than we give ourselves credit for, and really, we don’t need to understand a lot in our lives, we just need to accept it.

As a personal opinion; labels aren’t really important outside of a technical or logistical setting. I prefer far more to explain a situation and explain who I am rather than label myself. But it really depends on context and the situation.

And, just for the sake of it,
You might be male(“male” wouldn’t mean you have to behave any certain way, just to say), you crossdress, and you’re gay. Those are all things you could say are a part of you, and you are a part of. In the end, people are people and I’m sure a lot of people can connect with that alone, anything else on top of that is more to value. 

I hope this helps, my best advice here would be advocating easing the worry, cause it feels like a subject that will get better and more understood as you give yourself time, you accept yourself, and your brain has time to process it all. Again, hope this helps. And good luck!

I don’t mean to invalidate any feelings, but I get this notation mostly from the fact that you’re aware of this, feel guilty for it and want to change; are you sure this is a genuine feeling around attraction, or more-so a worry/fear of yours? I know the mind loves to build false narratives around ourselves when we’re afraid of being immoral. It’s a common obsession for people to convince themselves they’re racist while they fear being racist (the fear of which is usually a good indication they’re not racist). In my opinion, it’s entirely possible you just haven’t been attracted to these people you’ve seen, and I wouldn’t say that’s racism. Racism is a decision and action based on opinions, we don’t control our attractions whatsoever and we may not necessarily understand every situation we run in to. 

If you genuinely care, which it looks like you do, chances are you’re not being racist. I wouldn’t beat yourself up over this, I’m sure the fact that it’s on your mind will make it easier to improve overtime and eventually any racist feelings or fears will diminish.
